name: LegoZendo
author: chris (spec) / orchestrator (implementation)
description: Lego Zendo v3. Clue: capital letter x + number y in 0..12. Solution: an ASCII layout of 2-row x 3-column lego bricks (capital letters, any consistent non-letter filler). Bricks come in two orientations: 2 rows x 3 cols (pins up/down) and 3 rows x 2 cols (pins left/right); pins are always on the 3-stud side. A CONNECTION is two bricks of the SAME orientation adjacent along their pin axis (horizontal bricks: rows differ by 2, column overlap 1..3; vertical bricks: columns differ by 2, row overlap 1..3); the overlap is the pin width. Mixed-orientation contact never counts. No connectivity requirement: bricks may be scattered. EXACTLY y of the 1-pin connections must join two bricks of letter x. 2- and 3-pin x-x connections and 1-pin x-other connections are decoys. The scorer tiles letters greedily (horizontal 2x3 first, then vertical 3x2); solve() verifies its output with the same parse. solve() rejection-samples scattered/attached layouts (both orientations, 30-70% vertical) until the width histogram is near-uniform (each width 27-40%) and there are >= 5y connections (so contributing connections are <= 20%), then assigns letters (>= 5 distinct) to meet the count, adding decoy x bricks joined only by 2/3-pin edges. Human-designed rule; a test of invented rules vs model priors.
